**Why did M2 become better at low [S]?**
- At low [S], the reaction is **substrate-limited**, so the kinetic profile is more sensitive to the **catalyst state** (monomer vs. dimer)
- At high [S], both mechanisms can fit the data similarly because substrate saturation masks the difference
- M2's dimerization equilibrium (2cat ⇌ cat2) becomes more apparent when substrate is limiting

If M18 is correct, we should see **linear dependence on [cat]** with deactivation effects.

Alternatively, I could test **product inhibition** to distinguish M2 from M18, since M18 involves substrate-dependent deactivation while M2 does not.

I will choose to **vary catalyst concentration** to test the order of dependence.

  - **Prediction**: Initial rate should depend **linearly on [cat]** (simple Michaelis-Menten with substrate cooperativity)
